replies.text:
Check of commonly-missed items:
- Automated abuse (sign-in brute force, email/SMS flooding, mass sign-up, scraping): design mentions only "PATCH /users/{id} accepts a JSON body" — no authentication form, no messaging, no read/list endpoint stated. Not present.
- Staff/admin screens showing user-supplied content: no admin UI or content rendering in the design ("Users call it to update their display name" is the only UI-adjacent text). Not present.
- Privileged actions with no record (role change, status change): present — "copies every field onto the user record, including fields like role and accountStatus". Not covered by the agreed list (threats 1–4 are all escalation/tampering outcomes, none addresses accountability for the privilege change).
- Cacheable personal/account pages: no GET of personal documents or pages described. Not present.
- Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, CSV/exports, emails, headers: design states no export, email, or log sink. Not present.
- Single-reviewer threat 2 (email overwrite → account recovery takeover): duplicate of agreed threat 4. Excluded.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-08",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["PATCH /users/{id} handler", "user record store"],
    "dataStores": ["user record"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["client -> user update API"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "Role and accountStatus changes leave no distinct record of who made them",
      "scenario": "The same handler path serves a display-name edit and a change to role or accountStatus, because every field in the body is copied onto the user record. No separate record of a privilege or status change is described, so after a user grants themselves admin or reactivates a suspended account, responders cannot tell which records were altered, by whom, or what the prior values were. An insider who legitimately reaches the endpoint can also alter a user's role and later deny doing so.",
      "component": "PATCH /users/{id} handler",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 2,
      "rating": { "attacker": "insider", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "minor" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "PATCH /users/{id} accepts a JSON body and copies every field onto the user record, including fields like role and accountStatus." },
        { "quote": "Users call it to update their display name." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.1.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "Changing someone's role or account status looks exactly like renaming a profile, so nobody can see who changed privileges or undo it.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Audit privilege and status changes separately from profile edits",
        "given": "a request to PATCH /users/{id} that changes role or accountStatus",
        "when": "the change is applied to the user record",
        "then": "an immutable audit entry records the acting identity, target user id, field, old and new values and timestamp, distinct from ordinary profile-field edits"
      }
    }
  ]
}
